properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 23 at 3:29AM CST until November 23 at 10:00AM CST by NWS Duluth MN
properties.description:
* WHAT...Lake effect snow. Additional snow accumulations up to two
inches.

* WHERE...Iron County.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM CST this morning.

* IMPACTS...Plan on slippery road conditions. The hazardous
conditions will impact the Monday morning commute.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Blustery northwest winds gusting 20 to 25 mph
combined with falling snow may cause visibility to fall below 1
mile at times during the Monday morning commute.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. Call 511 or visit
www.511wi.gov for Wisconsin road information.

Lake effect snow bands and showers are expected to create conditions
ranging from locally heavy snow to dry weather just a few miles away.
Visibilities can also vary greatly. Be prepared for rapid changes in
weather, visibility, and road conditions.

properties.headline: Storm Warning issued November 23 at 1:08AM PST until November 24 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...South winds 25 to 30 kt with gusts up to 35 kt and
steep seas 12 to 14 ft at 13 seconds through tonight. South
winds increase late tonight to gales 30 to 40 kt with gusts up
to 50 kt with very steep and hazardous seas 18 to 23 ft at 12
seconds expected. South winds increase again late Monday night
with storm force winds of 40 to 50 kt with gusts 55 to 60 kt.
Seas will become very steep and chaotic 23 to 28 ft at 13
seconds.

* WHERE...All areas.

* WHEN...For the Small Craft Advisory, until 7 AM PST Monday.
For the Gale Warning, from 7 AM Monday to 4 AM PST Tuesday.
For the Storm Warning, from 4 AM to 4 PM PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Very strong winds and very steep seas could capsize
or damage vessels. Visibilities will be significantly reduced.
properties.instruction:
Mariners should remain in port, alter course, and/or secure the
vessel for very strong winds and very steep and hazardous seas.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 23 at 4:06AM EST by NWS Blacksburg VA
properties.description:
Patchy dense fog and areas of drizzle remain in place across the
mountains and portions of the foothills this morning, resulting
in visibilities that may be as low as one hundred feet in spots.
These conditions are likely to persist through the morning
commute for some. Motorists are urged to drive at lower speeds
when encountering poor visibility, and to maintain extra
separation distance with surrounding vehicles. Leave a few minutes
early to allow yourself extra time to reach your destination
safely.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Small Craft Advisory, southeast winds 20 to 30 kt

35 kt.

* WHERE...Coastal Waters from Cape Flattery to Cape Shoalwater
out to 10 nm.

* WHEN...For the Small Craft Advisory, until 7 AM PST this
morning. For the Gale Warning, from 7 AM this morning to 3 PM
PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.
properties.instruction:

experience and properly equipped vessels. It is highly
recommended that mariners without the proper experience seek safe
harbor prior to the onset of gale conditions.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 23 at 1:14AM CST by NWS San Angelo TX
properties.description:
The combination of an upper level storm system, increasing
moisture and temperatures in the 30s may produce a few hours of
light snow mainly west of a Sterling City to Throckmorton line
Tuesday morning. Expect little to no accumulation of snowfall.
However, there is a low chance of local accumulations around 1/2
of an inch which may cause a few slick spots on roads. The rest of
west central Texas will only see rain showers Tuesday morning.
Keep up with the latest weather information this week.

Also, expect colder temperatures across the area. A widespread
freeze is expected Wednesday morning with lows in the mid to upper
20s, possibly a few degrees colder in low lying areas and river
valleys. Highs will only be in the 40s Tuesday. Please prepare
for the colder weather.

properties.headline: Wind Advisory issued November 22 at 10:50PM PST until November 25 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Pendleton OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Dense Fog Advisory, visibility of one quarter mile
or less in dense fog and freezing fog. For the Wind Advisory for
the base and slopes of the northern Blue Mountains, southeast winds
25 to 35 mph with gusts of 40 to 55 mph expected.

* WHERE...Foothills of the Northern Blue Mountains of Oregon.

* WHEN...For the Dense Fog Advisory, until 11 AM PST Monday. For the
Wind Advisory, from 7 PM Monday to 4 AM PST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result. Low
visibility could make driving conditions hazardous.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Winds will be lighter away from the base of
the Blue Mountains.
properties.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

If driving, slow down, use your headlights, and leave plenty of
distance ahead of you.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Del Norte; Southwestern Humboldt; Coastal Mendocino
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 22 at 10:49PM PST until November 26 at 2:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Watch, High astronomical tides
and large surf with storm surge may cause moderate flooding in
low lying areas along the Redwood/Mendocino Coast. Up to one
foot of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in
low lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal
Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...From Tuesday morning through Thursday afternoon during
periods of high tide.

* IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying
property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated.
Some shoreline erosion may occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Expect continued increases in high tide
water levels through the coming work week with the tide
peaking on Wednesday. Prepare now and pay attention to
official guidance on shelters and or resources available to
the public.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Watch means that flooding is possible but not
imminent. Coastal residents in the watch area should begin
preparations for rising water and take appropriate action to
protect life and property.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

NWSheadline: COASTAL FLOOD WATCH REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM TUESDAY MORNING THROUGH THURSDAY AFTERNOON

properties.areaDesc: Northern Coastal Humboldt
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 22 at 10:49PM PST until November 23 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, High astronomical tides
and storm surge will cause moderate flooding in low lying areas
along the Humboldt Bay Coast. Up to 1.5 to 2.0 feet of saltwater
inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. Between 9.3 and 9.8 feet
MLLW at the North Spit tide gauge is predicted. For the Coastal
Flood Watch, High astronomical tides and large surf with storm
surge may cause moderate flooding in low lying areas along the
Redwood/Mendocino Coast. Up to 2 feet of saltwater inundation
above ground level is possible in low lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 7 AM to noon PST
Monday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Monday afternoon
through Thursday afternoon. High tide is at 9:44 AM at the
Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will
be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high tide.

* IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying
property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated.
These impacts will include, but not limited to, roadways in
King Salmon and the Arcata bottoms/sections of highway 101
Shoreline erosion will occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Expect continued increases in high tide
water levels through the coming work week with the tide
peaking on Wednesday. Prepare now and pay attention to
official guidance on shelters and or resources available to
the public.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Warning means that flooding is occurring or
imminent. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert
for rising water and take appropriate action to protect life and
property.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

properties.description:

* WHERE...East facing reefs of the Marianas.

* WHEN...Through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A trade-wind swell will continue to produce
a high risk of rip currents along east-facing reefs. Surf along
east-facing reefs will also be elevated with the rip current
risk along north-facing reefs also elevated.

current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 22 at 7:05PM PST until November 24 at 4:00AM PST by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding
expected.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 AM PST Tuesday.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 4 AM Tuesday to 1 PM PST
Friday. Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the
time of the morning high tide, with peak tides trending from 7
AM on Monday to 10 AM on Friday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides peak Tuesday through
Wednesday, reaching 7.9-8.3 feet, likely re-breaking the all-
time tidal records set back in late October. Background surf
on top of the tides will remain around 3-5 feet through
Wednesday, but an incoming swell Wednesday into Thursday will
bring a sharp increase to the surf by Thursday morning's high
tide. Breaking waves may reach 6-8 feet with sets up to 10
feet on west-facing beaches. Surf then moderates some into
Friday, but still looks to be around 5-8 feet.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

are forecast to reach a crest tonight before beginning a very slow
decline within Major flood stage later in the week.

For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Major
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
The river has surpassed its previous record flood.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 10.8 feet, Water covers State Road 46 and it may
become impassable near Jungle Road and Prevatt Road. Standing water
on secondary roads near the river deepens to more than three feet
in some areas. Flooding becomes more significant to structures and
marinas from above Lake Harney to the Lake Jesup area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 AM EST Sunday the stage was 12.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 AM EST Sunday was 12.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 13.1 feet
tonight. The river is then forecast to begin a slow decline
through this week.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.

properties.areaDesc: Mason, WA
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued November 22 at 3:44PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
ESFSEW

A series of weather systems will bring heavy precipitation to the
Olympic Peninsula starting this week. Snow levels will rise to around
5000 feet or higher, allowing this to be primarily in the form of
rain from Tuesday onward. This will bring 3 to 4 inches of rain to
the Olympics this week, leading to significant rises on the Skokomish
River in Mason County. Any snowfall in the upper portions of the
basin through Monday will likely add to additional runoff. Flooding
is currently expected as early as late Wednesday and may continue
until the weekend.

Please monitor the latest river forecasts from the National Weather
Service for additional information.

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 22 at 2:23PM PST until November 26 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 2.0 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Coastal Flood
Warning, significant coastal flooding with up to 2.8 feet of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Warning,
Dangerously large breaking waves of 20 to 30 feet.

* WHERE...San Francisco County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST Monday.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM Monday to 4 PM PST
Thursday. For the High Surf Warning, from midnight Tuesday
night to midnight PST Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, numerous road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the
highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tide gauge,
high tide is expected to be 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW)
at 9:25 AM Monday, 2.6 ft above normal (8.4 ft MLLW) at 10:05 AM
Tuesday, 2.8 ft above normal (8.6 ft MLLW) at 10:49 AM
Wednesday, and 2.4 ft above normal (8.2 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM
Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.6 ft of surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High
tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific
Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.

properties.areaDesc: South Central Oregon Coast; Curry County Coast
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 22 at 1:33PM PST until November 26 at 7:00PM PST by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, higher than normal
astronomical tides (King Tides) are expected to bring up to 2.4
ft of inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways on Monday. For the Coastal Flood
Warning, higher than normal astronomical tides (King Tides)
combined with storm surge from large surf are expected to bring
up to 3.1 ft of inundation above ground level Tuesday and
Wednesday, with up to 2.6 ft of inundation expected on Thursday.

* WHERE...Beaches and low lying areas along the shore lines of
Douglas, Coos and Curry Counties. This includes the communities
of North Bend, Charleston, Port Orford, Gold Beach, and Coos
Bay. Coastal flooding is expected to impact portions of Highway
101 around Gold Beach, Coos Bay, and Reedsport.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 7 AM to 4 PM PST
Monday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 7 AM Tuesday to 7
PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. This event
is expected see similar impacts to what occurred on January
3rd, 2026.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The worst conditions are expected to be
during the high tide periods in the late morning/early
afternoon. This is especially so for Tuesday and Wednesday as
storm activity brings large breaking surf heights of 23 to 28 ft
and adds storm surge to the water levels. Storm activity
lessens on Thursday, but King Tides will still be present, which
will likely continue inundation impacts. At the Charleston, OR
tide gauge, high tide is expected to be at 10:09 AM Monday, at
10:51 AM Tuesday, at 11:35 AM Wednesday, and at 12:23 PM
Thursday.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

properties.headline: High Wind Warning issued November 22 at 12:20PM PST until November 24 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Wind Advisory, south winds 20 to 35 mph with gusts
up to 55 mph expected. For the High Wind Warning, south winds 30 to
45 mph with gusts up to 65 mph expected.

* WHERE...Most of the Shasta Valley in central Siskiyou County. This
includes portions of Interstate 5 as well as the communities of
Weed, Gazelle, Grenada and Montague.

* WHEN...For the Wind Advisory, from noon Monday to 4 AM PST Tuesday.
For the High Wind Warning, from 4 AM to 10 PM PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Damaging winds could blow down trees, power lines, and
unsecured objects. Power outages are possible. Travel could be
difficult, especially for high profile vehicles.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highways and roads running west to east,
including highway 97, will be exposed to tough driving conditions
given the strong southerly wind speeds. Winds are expected to be
strongest late Tuesday morning through Tuesday afternoon.
properties.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

People are urged to secure loose objects, including large or
inflatable holiday decorations that could be blown around or damaged
by the wind.

difficult, especially for high profile vehicles.

inflatable holiday decorations that could be blown around or damaged
by the wind.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by an upstream dam release is expected.

* WHERE...Central Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 315 PM MST Friday Nov 27.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 313 PM MST, a streamflow gauge has indicated that water from
an upstream dam release from Painted Rock Dam has reached
Dateland. Flooding is expected along the Gila River within the
warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.
